comments.note: OWASP Full Review — No Critical or High findings. All 10 OWASP categories reviewed: A01 (Broken Access Control): PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX (/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$/) is anchored at both ends, preventing path traversal (../evil) in handleDeleteKnowledge and handlePromoteKnowledge. The storage layer has a defence-in-depth _validateSlug() call in repositoryStorePath(). No IDOR or privilege-escalation paths found. A02 (Cryptographic Failures): No cryptographic operations, no secrets, no credentials. N/A. A03 (Injection): All user-supplied inputs (scope, repository_name, rawId, body) pass through Zod schemas or explicit regex guards before reaching the filesystem. No SQL, template, or command injection surfaces. Validated. A04 (Insecure Design): Guard placement is correct in both handlers — presence check precedes format check, no bypass possible. Double-validation at handler + storage layer is defence-in-depth, not a design flaw. A05 (Security Misconfiguration): validationError() uses structured ApiError with a controlled message — no internal paths or stack traces leaked to callers. A06 (Vulnerable & Outdated Components): No new dependencies introduced in this WP. Only zod (already present) is used. A07 (Auth/Authentication Failures): Auth/authz is handled upstream (server.ts / middleware). Handler layer correctly assumes authenticated context. No auth regressions introduced. A08 (Software & Data Integrity): atomicWriteJson + withLock ensure write integrity; Zod parse-before-write guards all store mutations. A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring): Validation failures throw ApiError — HTTP 400 responses are observable by upstream logging middleware. No silent swallowing of security-relevant errors. A10 (SSRF): No HTTP/URL fetching in the affected code. Filesystem paths are fully constructed from controlled prefixes (ledgerRoot) + validated slugs. No SSRF surface.

Info — A01 / Input Validation: In handleListKnowledge, the repository_name query parameter (line ~193) is forwarded to KnowledgeStoreManager.listInsights() and ultimately to repositoryStorePath() without being validated against PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX at the handler level. The storage layer's _validateSlug() provides a defence-in-depth guard and will throw before any file access occurs, so no exploitation path exists. However, the thrown error from the storage layer will propagate as an unhandled Error (HTTP 500) rather than a typed ApiError (HTTP 400), which is a minor inconsistency in the API contract. Not a blocking finding — no security impact. Recommendation: add an explicit PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX guard for repository_name in handleListKnowledge (mirrors the pattern now in place for delete/promote), converting the potential HTTP 500 into a clean HTTP 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

Info — A03 / Injection: The search query in handleListKnowledge (params.query) is passed as a plain substring to searchInsights(), which applies .toLowerCase().includes(q) against stored data. No regex is compiled from user input, so there is no ReDoS surface. Confirmed safe.

[documentation-forward] handleListKnowledge does not validate repository_name against PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX at the handler level (flagged by Security Auditor, confirmed during review). A malformed slug passed to this handler would propagate through to the storage layer's _validateSlug(), which throws a plain Error (HTTP 500) rather than a typed ApiError (HTTP 400). This inconsistency in the API contract should be documented as a known-limitation in the file-level JSDoc block until a follow-up WP adds the explicit guard (mirroring the pattern now in place for delete/promote). No security impact — the storage-layer guard prevents any file access.

The 4 new test cases (AC-1 through AC-4 rework) each invoke the handler twice with identical arguments — once to assert { code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' } and once to assert instanceof ApiError. While not wrong, combining both assertions into a single invocation with a variable holding the rejected error would be slightly more efficient and eliminate the redundant handler call. Low priority — no correctness issue.

The validationError() message for malformed repository_name ('repository_name contains invalid characters. Use only alphanumerics, hyphens, and underscores.') is slightly inconsistent with the PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX docstring, which also mentions digits and underscores but uses 'letters' rather than 'alphanumerics'. A future cleanup pass could align these wordings. Not blocking — both messages are accurate.
